title: Best Double Buggies UK
short: Six double buggies for twins and siblings, tested by parents over weeks across pavements, parks and rough terrain.
intro: Double buggies range from narrow side-by-sides to versatile tandems that convert from single to double, and the right choice depends on your doorways, boot space and terrain. This guide is based on Mumsnet's tested roundup (updated September 2026), which cross-checked Which? lab results and RoSPA safety advice, then had parent-testers use each buggy over weeks with their own children across more than 150 miles and a range of terrain. Prices shown are RRPs quoted by Mumsnet and vary by bundle.

products.name: Duet V4
products.best_for: Twins or siblings who need a narrow side-by-side that still fits through a standard front door
products.key_spec: Side by side, 63cm wide, birth to about 4 years, 22kg per seat, 10kg basket, adjustable handlebar
products.summary: Mumsnet's Best Buy. Twin dad Jonny used it daily for seven weeks with his newborn twins on pavements, in parks, shops, cafés and on the bus. Its narrow 63cm wheelbase, about the same as many single buggies, fitted through his standard front door without folding, and four air-filled tyres with rear suspension handled kerbs, hills and gravel with ease. Assembly instructions could be clearer, the folded frame took up most of his car boot, and a clicking sound developed around the brake during testing.
pros: Just 63cm wide, close to a single buggy
cons: Fold controls are at the front of the buggy
Folded frame takes up considerable boot space
Sun hoods could provide more coverage
products.search: Mountain Buggy Duet V4 double buggy

products.name: Evalite Duo Pushchair
products.best_for: Lightweight, affordable travel with cushioned seats and a lie-flat back seat for infants
products.key_spec: Tandem, newborn to 4 years, 11.24kg, one-handed fold, car seat compatible, no carrycot option
products.summary: Winner of Which?'s Best Lightweight Double Buggy award and a 2017 Red Dot Design award, at just over 11kg versus the average 13 to 15kg for double buggies. Its aluminium tandem frame manoeuvres well on pavements and narrow streets thanks to smooth four-wheel suspension with lockable front swivel wheels, though it's less suited to off-road terrain like woodland walks. Both seats have UPF50+ sun canopies, and it folds down tight enough to stand on its own. It's quite long with a gap between seats that takes getting used to, and the car seat is tricky to attach.
pros: Super lightweight for a double buggy
Large storage basket and good value for money
cons: Car seat is tricky to attach

products.name: Peach 7 Twin
products.best_for: Twin parents who want maximum configuration options in a slim tandem
products.key_spec: Tandem, newborn to 4 years (or 7 in single mode), 15kg per seat (25kg single mode), 12.9kg in double mode, up to 25 configurations
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Tara, a twin mum, loved the look of it, saying it's very aesthetically pleasing with comfy carrycots and good quality material. Now in its seventh generation, it converts between single, double and twin mode using an adaptor set, with a seat unit just 36cm wide so you can wheel a sleeping baby straight out the front door. The carrycot converts to a seat after six months. It's expensive, tricky to assemble with multiple zips, and the one-handed fold takes getting used to.
pros: Extremely versatile, with up to 25 configurations
Tandem design as narrow as a single pram
Large wheels roll over most surfaces with ease
cons: Tricky to assemble, with multiple zips
One-handed fold is hard to engage

products.name: City Tour 2 Double
products.best_for: Urban families who want the lightest double buggy that still fits two carrycots
products.key_spec: Side by side, newborn to 4 years, 10.5kg, 15kg per seat, two carrycots optional, compact fold
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Liz, a mum of two, found it the lightest double buggy on their list at 10.5kg and only 66.5cm wide, geared towards urban life and fitting through most doorways. It offers two world-facing seats from birth or two parent-facing carrycots, with infinite recline and a reliable footbrake that Liz found secure even on hills. Bumper bars and a rain cover aren't included, the harness is fiddly, and it's not travel system-compatible.
pros: Cosy carrycot option and compact fold
cons: Small wheels don't cope well with rough terrain
Rain cover and bumper bars not included

products.name: Nipper Double V6
products.best_for: Muddy park paths, countryside walks and steep city streets with two children
products.key_spec: Side by side (three-wheel), newborn to about 4 years, 22kg per seat, 12-inch air-filled tyres, handlebar-mounted handbrake
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Brogan, a twin mum, found the seats particularly roomy, even with her 3.5-year-old twins nearing the buggy's upper age limit. Three large air-filled tyres and rear suspension glide over grass, gravel and uneven ground, and a lightweight aluminium frame keeps it manageable with two children aboard. At around 71 to 72cm it's still slim enough for most doorways. It's not travel system-compatible, isn't the most compact when folded, and is bulky for public transport.
pros: Rain cover and removable storage basket included
products.search: Out n About Nipper Double V6

products.name: Donkey 6
products.best_for: Families who start with one child and want to add a second seat later
products.key_spec: Side by side, converts single to double, birth to about 4 years, 22kg per seat, reversible seats, adjustable handlebar
products.summary: Mumsnet found it smooth and easy to manoeuvre and sturdy across different surfaces, with the flexibility to run as a single buggy and convert to a double when a second child arrives. Comfortable, reversible seats and generous storage make it work well for a newborn and toddler together. It's heavy to lift at over 19kg fully assembled, doesn't fit through every doorway, is awkward on public transport, takes up most of a small boot, and needs a multi-step fold with seats removed for a compact fold.

specs.Orientation: Side by side, converts single to double

pros: Comfortable, reversible seats and generous storage
cons: Doesn't fit through every doorway, awkward on public transport
Takes up most of a small car boot, multi-step fold

guide.a: Side-by-side buggies like the Mountain Buggy Duet and Baby Jogger City Tour 2 give both children the same view and are easier to load evenly, but can be wide for doorways. Tandem buggies like the Joie Evalite Duo and iCandy Peach 7 are narrower, often close to a single buggy's width, but the seats sit at different distances from the ground.

guide.q: Will it fit through my front door?
guide.a: Check the width carefully. The Mountain Buggy Duet is just 63cm wide, close to a single buggy, and its tester found it fit through his standard front door without folding. Wider side-by-sides and the Bugaboo Donkey 6 may not fit through every doorway.

For grass, gravel and uneven paths, Mumsnet's testers rated the Out 'n' About Nipper Double V6 and Mountain Buggy Duet V4 highly, both using large air-filled tyres and suspension. Lighter travel-focused buggies like the Joie Evalite Duo and Baby Jogger City Tour 2 are better suited to pavements and city life.

guide.q: Do I need a double buggy from birth, or can it grow with me?
guide.a: The Bugaboo Donkey 6 and iCandy Peach 7 both start as a single buggy and expand for a second child, useful if your children aren't twins. Most others here, including the Mountain Buggy Duet and Nipper Double, are built as double buggies from the outset and take carrycots for newborns on both sides.
